text:
sanjay: Seeing a spike of tiny GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 this morning. ~120 evictions over 10m, most are 'taint not tolerated' after warm-pool nodes came up. Logs show node gets tainted -> scheduler reschedules -> warm-pool agent clears taint but too late and pods already preempted.

katie: ugh. tl;dr impact? customer-facing? :eyes:

sanjay: Latency for some short inference jobs doubled until they rescheduled. A few internal nightly CI runs failed. No customer data loss but higher cost because pods landed on on-demand nodes.

mike: do we have the exact taint key? can you paste the node event?

sanjay: here's a snippet: 
```
Node/node-aps1-12    TaintAdded      reason=WarmPoolReserve controller=warmpool-agent taint=warm-reserve=true:NoSchedule
Pod/predictor-xyz    FailedScheduling reason=TolerationsNotFound
// then warmpool-agent removed taint ~18s later
```

dana: 18s is enough for scheduler to give up and place elsewhere. We should either: reduce taint lifetime, make warmpool-agent remove taint faster, or have scheduler consider a temporary soft-toleration window.

katie: can we flip to using PreferNoSchedule instead of NoSchedule while we fix agent latency? :thinking_face:

mike: PreferNoSchedule helps but doesn't stop preemptive binpack decisions when on-demand capacity is available. Also pod eviction churn increases cost. I'd prefer increasing warmpool node readiness probe parallelism so agent can untaint faster.

sanjay: created a quick Canary: bump agent threads on ap-southeast1 warmpool from 2->6, and change taint TTL logic to 5s max. rolling now.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 1711112235 - ap-southeast1 evict-rate 9/m (threshold 5/m) - triggered autoscale fallback to on-demand.

dana: also adding a short-lived scheduling predicate tweak: if node taint key==warm-reserve and node.age < 60s, treat as transient. Will prototype as k8s scheduler extension.

katie: ping me if the Canary looks good, want to run cost calc for worst-case on-demand bleed.

sanjay: Canary reduced evictions to 1/m after 3min. cost bleed estimated ~+$180/hr during peak without fix. I'll open a ticket to make agent change permanent + scheduler tweak RFC.

mike: nice. followups: add metrics for taint add/remove delta, instrument scheduler decision logs, and alert on eviction->on-demand landing ratio.

dana: noted. I'll draft RFC for transient-taint policy and link to ticket.

katie: thanks team :thumbsup:
